title_en: Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate v. Ding Likang — bribery case
ruling_gist_en: In state-owned medical institutions, administrative personnel with public service status who engage in information management work such as medical data statistics, transmission, and maintenance, and whose statistics, transmission, and maintenance information and data are important bases for the management, supervision, and decision-making of medical services by state-owned medical institutions, and thus constitute medical insurance information, and whose work content has a public service nature, such personnel are persons engaged in public service in state-owned institutions and shall be regarded as state functionaries. Where such personnel, by taking advantage of their official duties in information management, illegally accept property from pharmaceutical marketing personnel and provide them with statistical data on drug usage in the medical institution and other information, thereby facilitating the sale of drugs by related drug manufacturers and sales enterprises through improper means, their conduct shall be convicted and punished for the crime of bribery in accordance with the provisions of Article 385, paragraph (1) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate v. Ding Likang — bribery case

Ruling Summary

Where a person with establishment (bianzhi) status in a state-owned medical institution is engaged in information management such as medical data statistics, transmission, and maintenance, and the information and data he/she transmits and maintains constitute important bases for the management, supervision, and decision-making of medical services by the state-owned medical institution, such information falls within the category of medical insurance information, and the nature of the work is official. Such person is a person engaged in public service in a state-owned institution and shall be treated as a state functionary. Where such person, by taking advantage of his/her position in information management, illegally accepts property from pharmaceutical marketing personnel, provides them with statistical data on the usage of drugs in the institution, and thereby facilitates the marketing of drugs by relevant pharmaceutical producers and sellers through improper means, the act shall be convicted and punished as the crime of bribery in accordance with Article 385, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Procuratorial Authority: Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Ding Likang, male, 35 years old, Han ethnicity, college degree, formerly the information manager of the office of the Shanghai Jiading District Malu Town Community Health Service Center, residing in Shanghai Jiading Industrial Zone. Released on bail pending trial in this case on May 24, 2011.

The Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate instituted a public prosecution against Ding Likang for the crime of bribery before the Shanghai Jiading District People's Court.

The indictment alleged: During his tenure as information manager of the office of the Shanghai Jiading District Malu Town Community Health Service Center, the defendant, Ding Likang, took advantage of his duties in building and maintaining computer networks and conducting daily statistical work. From 2006 to 2011, he separately accepted kickbacks totaling RMB 49,000 (all amounts hereinafter in RMB) from Xu Rong, Zhang Hanqiu, Wu Yinbing, and others, as follows: 1. From 2006 to 2011, he successively accepted kickbacks totaling RMB 27,600 from Xu Rong, a sales representative for Felodipine tablets, Shangshi Zhitong Gao (traumatic injury analgesic plaster), and other pharmaceuticals; 2. From the second half of 2007 to March/April 2011, he successively accepted kickbacks totaling approximately RMB 20,000 from Zhang Hanqiu, a pharmaceutical sales representative for Zhejiang Hailisheng Company; 3. From 2008 to 2010, he accepted gift vouchers and prepaid cards worth a total of RMB 2,000 on three occasions from Wu Yinbing, the head of Shanghai Yinbing Trade Co., Ltd., a supplier of computer equipment. After receiving a circular on May 17, 2011, from the Anti-Corruption Bureau of the Shanghai People's Procuratorate regarding clues on bribery cases in the city's medical system, the Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate discovered that Ding Likang was suspected of bribery and initiated a preliminary investigation on May 18, 2011. On the morning of May 23, 2011, when summoned for a talk by the Malu Town Community Health Service Center, Ding Likang voluntarily confessed to his unit the criminal facts of accepting bribes from relevant pharmaceutical sales representatives. That same afternoon, when summoned for an interview with the procuratorial authorities, Ding Likang also truthfully confessed the above criminal facts. The prosecutorial authority alleged that Ding Likang, as a state functionary, took advantage of his position to seek benefits for others and accepted bribes totaling over RMB 49,000, thereby violating the provisions of Article 385, paragraph 1, Article 386, and Article 383, paragraph 1, item (3) and paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, and should be prosecuted for the crime of bribery. Ding Likang had the circumstance of voluntary surrender and, according to Article 67, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, could be given a lighter punishment. The case was submitted for trial according to law.

The defendant, Ding Likang, argued that he had accepted only over RMB 18,000 in kickbacks from Zhang Hanqiu, and that part of the gift vouchers and prepaid cards from Wu Yinbing were given because Ding had usually helped Wu with computer-related consultations. He had no objection to the remaining criminal facts and evidence charged by the prosecutorial authority and requested the court to give him a lighter punishment.

After trial at first instance, the Shanghai Jiading District People's Court found: During his tenure as information manager of the office of the Shanghai Jiading District Malu Town Community Health Service Center, the defendant, Ding Likang, took advantage of his duties in building and maintaining computer networks and conducting daily statistical work. From 2006 to 2011, he accepted kickbacks totaling RMB 27,600 from Xu Rong, a sales representative for Felodipine tablets, Shangshi Zhitong Gao, and other pharmaceuticals. From the second half of 2007 to March/April 2011, he accepted kickbacks totaling over RMB 18,000 from Zhang Hanqiu, a pharmaceutical sales representative for Zhejiang Hailisheng Pharmaceutical Company, and provided the above pharmaceutical sales representatives with information on the usage of drugs in the hospital. From 2008 to 2010, he accepted gift vouchers and prepaid cards worth a total of RMB 2,000 from Wu Yinbing, the head of Shanghai Yinbing Trade Co., Ltd., a supplier of computer equipment. On May 23, 2011, when summoned for a talk by the leaders of his unit, Ding Likang voluntarily confessed the criminal facts of accepting bribes from relevant pharmaceutical sales representatives. That same day, when summoned for an interview with the procuratorial authorities, Ding Likang also truthfully confessed the above criminal facts. During the first instance proceedings, Ding Likang made a restitution payment of RMB 50,000.

The above facts were confirmed by evidence that was presented and cross-examined at trial, including the testimony of witnesses Xu Rong, Zhang Hanqiu, and Wu Yinbing; the Organization Code Certificate, Annual Assessment Registration Form, Employment Contract, Position Certificate, Job Responsibilities of Information System Administrator of the Information Department, relevant emails sent from Ding Likang's email account dingdong3800@163.com, detailed transaction records of an Agricultural Bank of China card, a certificate issued by the Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate, and the confession of the defendant Ding Likang. The evidence was sufficient to establish the facts.

The main issue at trial at first instance was: how to characterize the defendant Ding Likang's act.

The Shanghai Jiading District People's Court held at first instance:

The essential characteristic of a state functionary is exercising authority and engaging in public service, i.e., performing duties of organization, leadership, supervision, and management on behalf of state organs, state-owned companies, enterprises, institutions, people's organizations, etc. The defendant, Ding Likang, was originally the information manager of the office of the Shanghai Jiading District Malu Town Community Health Service Center. His duties included building and maintaining computer networks and conducting daily statistical work. His provision of information on relevant drug usage in the hospital to pharmaceutical sales representatives constituted taking advantage of work-related convenience that did not involve authority. This was not of a public service nature. Therefore, he should not be treated as a state functionary. His act constituted the crime of accepting bribes by a non-state functionary and should be punished according to law. As for his act of accepting gift vouchers and prepaid cards worth RMB 2,000 from the computer equipment supplier, the court, taking into account the fact that he had illegally accepted over RMB 47,000 in kickbacks from others, considered this in sentencing. The prosecutorial authority's opinion that Ding Likang had the circumstance of voluntary surrender and had surrendered the illicit gains, which could be grounds for a lighter punishment, was legally valid and supported by the court.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 163, paragraph 1, Article 67, paragraph 1, Article 72, paragraph 1, Article 73, paragraphs 2 and 3, Article 64 of the Criminal Law of the PRC and Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Cases of Voluntary Surrender and Meritorious Service, the Shanghai Jiading District People's Court rendered the following judgment on December 21, 2012:

1. The defendant, Ding Likang, was convicted of the crime of accepting bribes by a non-state functionary and sentenced to one year and nine months' imprisonment, suspended for one year and nine months;
2. The illicit gains were to be confiscated.

The Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate filed a protest with the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court on the grounds that the original judgment contained an error in the characterization of the crime, leading to an incorrect application of law and an obviously inappropriate sentence. During the second instance proceedings, the court appointed defense counsel Zheng Juping, a lawyer from Shanghai Guohe Law Firm, for Ding Likang.

The grounds for protest by the Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate were as follows: The Shanghai Jiading District Malu Town Community Health Service Center is a state-owned institution, and Ding Likang was a staff member with establishment (bianzhi) status in that institution. As the office information manager, Ding Likang's job responsibilities had a dual nature combining technical and managerial functions. Among these, Ding Likang's duty to manage, monitor, and maintain the confidentiality of drug usage data and other information within the hospital was essentially a duty of managing and supervising public affairs. Therefore, Ding Likang engaged in public service. The first instance judgment only noted the technical aspect of information management work but ignored its public affairs management aspect. The reason pharmaceutical sales representatives gave money to Ding Likang was that the drug usage data he provided enabled them to gain a competitive advantage in the market, which was essentially obtaining economic benefits through improper means. Ding Likang, by taking advantage of the authority conferred by the hospital, provided the relevant drug usage data, accepted money, and sought benefits for the pharmaceutical sales representatives, which met the essence of the crime of bribery. The Shanghai No. 2 Branch of the People's Procuratorate presented and read out the testimony of witness Lü Ying at trial, asserting that the protest by the Shanghai Jiading District People's Procuratorate was correct and should be supported. The existing evidence demonstrated that Ding Likang, as the office information manager of a state-owned institution, in addition to technical services such as computer and network management, also had duties such as assisting the relevant departments of the center in managing and statistically analyzing medical information and ensuring the security of such data. The work he performed was the foundation of the supervision and management functions of the hospital and the medical insurance department, and had a public service nature. His act of accepting money from pharmaceutical sales representatives met the constituent elements of the crime of bribery. The first instance court's finding that Ding Likang took advantage of work-related convenience without authority and that his act was not of a public service nature, thereby characterizing his act as the crime of accepting bribes by a non-state functionary, was an error in characterization that led to an incorrect application of law and an inappropriate sentence. The court was requested to correct the judgment according to law.

The defendant at first instance, Ding Likang, did not object to the first instance judgment. The appointed defense counsel argued that Ding Likang had taken advantage of work convenience by providing information indirectly related to his work to pharmaceutical sales representatives. The first instance characterization of the crime as accepting bribes by a non-state functionary was correct. Ding Likang did not actively solicit bribes; he accepted kickbacks out of a weak legal awareness. He also had circumstances of voluntary surrender and restitution of illicit gains, and showed repentance. The court was requested to give Ding Likang a lighter punishment and impose a suspended sentence.

After trial at second instance, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

The defendant at first instance, Ding Likang, was a staff member with establishment (bianzhi) status in a state-owned institution, the Shanghai Jiading District Malu Town Community Health Service Center. As the office information manager, Ding Likang's job responsibilities included monitoring the use of the information database, managing user permissions, assisting relevant departments in information management such as the statistical analysis and transmission of medical insurance data, and being responsible for the authenticity, accuracy, and security of the data. This information was an important basis for the state-owned hospital to manage, supervise, and make decisions regarding medical services. Ding Likang's management and monitoring of drug usage data and other medical insurance information in the hospital constituted the performance of duties of managing and supervising public affairs. The activities he engaged in were of a public service nature. Therefore, he should be treated as a state functionary. Ding Likang, as a state functionary engaged in public service in a state-owned institution, took advantage of his authority in information management to privately provide data to pharmaceutical dealers and accept money. This act met the characteristics of a money-for-power exchange in the crime of bribery. He also took advantage of his position having the authority to make recommendations on the procurement of computers for the unit, and in the course of daily network maintenance and management, accepted gift vouchers and prepaid cards from the computer equipment supplier. The relevant amounts should be aggregated with the aforementioned bribes accepted from pharmaceutical sales representatives, and he should be convicted of bribery as a single offense. The original judgment correctly found the acts and amounts of bribes accepted by Ding Likang, but the characterization of the crime was erroneous, leading to an incorrect application of law and an inappropriate sentence, which should be corrected according to law. The opinions of the protesting authority and the Shanghai No. 2 Branch of the People's Procuratorate were correct. Ding Likang voluntarily surrendered and truthfully confessed his crimes, constituting voluntary surrender. After the case came to light, he surrendered the illicit gains and showed repentance. The court adopted the opinion of the appointed defense counsel to give Ding a lighter punishment and impose a suspended sentence.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 225, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 385, paragraph 1, Article 386, Article 383, paragraph 1, item (3) and paragraph 2, Article 93, paragraph 2, Article 67, paragraph 1, Article 72, paragraph 1, Article 73, paragraphs 2 and 3, and Article 64 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on May 17, 2013:

1. The second item of the Criminal Judgment (2012) Jia Xing Chu Zi No. 1117 of the Shanghai Jiading District People's Court, namely the confiscation of illicit gains, was affirmed;
2. The first item of the Criminal Judgment (2012) Jia Xing Chu Zi No. 1117 of the Shanghai Jiading District People's Court, namely the conviction of the defendant Ding Likang for the crime of accepting bribes by a non-state functionary and sentencing him to one year and nine months' imprisonment, suspended for one year and nine months, was reversed;
3. The defendant at first instance, Ding Likang, was convicted of the crime of bribery and sentenced to three years' imprisonment, suspended for three years.

This judgment is final.
